name: Thea Energy
description: Thea Energy is reimagining how fusion power gets built -- starting with a fundamental rethink of the magnet. Spun out of Princeton University and the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory, the company is developing a stellarator, a type of fusion device that can run in a continuous, stable state without sudden plasma disruptions that have long plagued its better-known cousin, the tokamak. Traditional stellarators achieve that stability through magnets with elaborate, custom-sculpted three-dimensional shapes. This has historically made stellarators impractical to manufacture and maintain at scale. Thea's key insight is to flip that logic: instead of building complexity into the physical shape of the magnets, they use arrays of simple, flat (planar) coils and let software do the heavy lifting. The result is a fusion system that is not only more stable, but dramatically easier to build, service, and replicate -- a critical ingredient for deploying fusion energy at real-world scale.

name: Type One Energy
description: Type One Energy was born from a dinner conversation at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where leading stellarator scientists decided to stop waiting for academia and build the next leap in fusion themselves. The founders didn't just study stellarators; they built five of them, including UW-Madison's HSX machine and Germany's Wendelstein 7-X, the world's largest. Their approach preserves the stellarator's defining feature (i.e., physically twisted, non-planar magnets that hold superheated plasma in a stable, continuous flow) but unlocks it with two modern breakthroughs: high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets that generate far stronger fields than conventional materials, and advances in supercomputing that enable plasma optimization at previously impossible precision. Together, these clear the barriers that kept stellarators confined to research labs for decades. The company is building Infinity One, an engineering verification platform at TVA's Bull Run Energy Complex in Tennessee, scheduled for 2029, followed by Infinity Two, a 400-megawatt commercial fusion power plant designed to put clean electricity on the grid.

name: Barocal
description: Barocal is replacing harmful refrigerants with high-efficiency solid-state cooling technology for the $500B global HVAC market. Cambridge-based Barocal is commercialising solid-state cooling using barocaloric materials, a breakthrough resulting from 15 years of research at the University of Cambridge. Instead of cycling high-GWP refrigerant gases like conventional systems, Barocal’s technology applies pressure to proprietary solid-state barocaloric materials to transfer heat. This eliminates refrigerant leakage and the emissions associated with it. Why we invested in Barocal The climate case : Cooling emits over 4 Gt CO₂e annually, accounting for more than 7% of global greenhouse gas emissions, which makes it one of the largest decarbonisation blind spots. These emissions come from HFC refrigerant leakage, which often have global warming potentials more than 1,000 times higher than CO₂, as well as from the energy intensity of cooling itself. Cooling demand is projected to triple by 2050 , further increasing these emissions. Barocal directly addresses both leakage and energy consumption by eliminating refrigerant gases entirely and delivering significantly higher efficiency than existing solutions. The business case : The global HVAC market is worth approximately $450 billion and is expected to grow to $577 billion by 2033. Barocal is initially focused on commercial chillers and data centre cooling, targeting some of the fastest-growing and most profitable segments. The company is working in collaboration with large OEMs to bring the technology to market. In addition to the emissions benefits, higher efficiency reduces energy costs and results in a lower total cost of ownership for customers. The team : Prof. Xavier Moya, Co-Founder and CEO, is a Professor of Materials Physics at the University of Cambridge and a globally recognised pioneer in caloric materials and barocalorics. He has authored more than 150 scientific publications with over 15,000 citations. He founded Barocal to commercialise his breakthrough research, funded by the Royal Society and the European Research Council. Dr. Giles Rodway, Co-Founder and CTO, brings decades of industrial R&D experience from the automotive sector and previously founded Spinetic, combining deep engineering expertise with proven entrepreneurial credibility. Website: https://barocal.com/ Founded 2019 Management Prof. Xavier Moya Dr. Giles Rodway Location Cambridge, UK Segment Industry World Fund Investment Stage

name: Hyperscale Power
description: HYPERSCALE POWER IS BUILDING THE NEXT GENERATION OF ELECTRIC POWER INFRASTRUCTURE. The Zurich-based deeptech company is developing compact solid-state transformers (SSTs) designed for the power demands of AI data centres, EV charging, and large-scale renewable energy systems. Hyperscale Power’s proprietary design is roughly 10× smaller than conventional transformers and uses around 90% less material, dramatically reducing deployment timelines from years to weeks. By leveraging high-frequency operation and advanced power electronics, the system achieves energy-conversion efficiencies of up to 98.5% – significantly higher than today’s solutions. With a clear efficiency, cost, and emissions advantage, Hyperscale Power is positioned to unlock faster electrification and power delivery for the infrastructure underpinning the next industrial era. Why we invested in Hyperscale Power The climate case: Electricity systems lose around 6–8% of generated power globally through transmission and conversion inefficiencies. At the same time, the rapid growth of AI compute, EV charging networks, and renewable power generation is dramatically increasing electricity demand. Hyperscale Power’s solid-state transformers offer up to 98.5% energy-conversion efficiency and enable more flexible, modular grid architectures that can integrate renewables more effectively. Even a 2% improvement in efficiency at hyperscale data-centre and grid level translates into millions of tonnes of avoided CO₂ emissions. The company’s compact design also reduces material usage by roughly 90%, lowering embodied emissions and supporting a more resource-efficient power infrastructure. The business case: Hyperscale Power is entering a rapidly expanding multi-billion-euro market driven by hyperscalers, electrification, and global investment in energy infrastructure. Transformer supply chains are currently strained, with lead times stretching to 18–24 months as demand for high-power systems accelerates. Hyperscale Power’s SST technology dramatically shortens deployment timelines while delivering higher efficiency and power density. This creates a compelling value proposition for data centres, EV charging networks, and renewable-energy operators that need faster, more efficient power conversion to meet growing electricity demands. The team: Hyperscale Power was founded in 2025 by Daniel Rothmund and Sami Pettersson, who each bring more than a decade of experience in solid-state transformers and medium-voltage high-power converters. Their deep technical expertise in power electronics and transformer architecture underpins the company’s proprietary design. Based in Zurich, the team benefits from close ties to Europe’s leading engineering ecosystem around ETH Zürich, positioning the company to attract top technical talent and rapidly bring its technology to market. name: LITHOSQUARE
description: Lithosquare is accelerating critical minerals discovery with AI-driven geological intelligence that addresses the global supply bottleneck. The Paris-based company helps mining companies identify, rank and advance high-potential copper, lithium and rare earth deposits, faster, with higher confidence and at a fraction of the traditional cost. What sets Lithosquare apart is its geology-first approach. Where most AI-exploration tools look for statistical patterns in historical data, Lithosquare reasons from the science of how deposits form. Its platform is built around a proprietary metallogeny ontology covering around 20 deposit types, developed and maintained by PhD metallogenists working alongside AI engineers. This allows the system to generate credible targets in greenfield areas where no historical training data exists, a capability that pattern matching approaches cannot replicate. Why we invested in Lithosquare The climate case: Only around 1 in 1,000 mineral exploration projects ever becomes a mine, yet global demand for copper, lithium and rare earths is accelerating as electrification and AI infrastructure intensify. Average mine development lead times have stretched to nearly 18 years, creating a critical gap between exploration decisions today and production needed in the 2030s and 2040s. Lithosquare directly addresses this bottleneck by accelerating high-confidence discovery in jurisdictions that can meet Western supply-chain resilience requirements. By bringing new reserves to market faster and from jurisdictions with stronger environmental standards, Lithosquare unblocks the materials supply that global electrification depends on. The business case: Global mineral exploration budgets have historically ranged between $12-15bn annually, with a portion allocated to target generation, data analytics and technical advisory. Lithosquare's asset-light, partnership-driven model captures exploration service revenues while retaining long-term economic upside through Net Smelter Return royalties on successful discoveries. The global royalty and streaming sector has a combined enterprise value of over $140bn. Early partnerships validate strong demand for AI-accelerated exploration workflows and demonstrate traction across both large-cap operators and mid-tier explorers. The team: Co-Founder and CEO Aymeric Preveral-Etcheverry previously scaled Fieldbox, an industrial AI company. COO Simon Leclair brings 15+ years of mining expertise, including early-career mine development work at Eramet and 8 years as a partner at BCG specialising in Metals and Mining strategy. Both are Mines Paris graduates, combining deep geological credibility with proven operational execution and AI expertise. Website: https://www.lithosquare.com/ Founded 2024 Management Aymeric Preveral-Etcheverry, Co-Founder & CEO Simon Leclair, Founding COO Location Paris, France Segment Industry / Critical Materials World Fund Investment Stage

name: NITRICITY
description: Nitricity is electrifying organic fertilizer production with a world-first, plant-based alternative that’s transforming agriculture. The US-based company has developed Ash Tea , a liquid organic nitrogen fertilizer made from recycled almond shells, air, water, and renewable energy. Fully vegan, pathogen-free, and cost-competitive, Ash Tea is already sold out for years to come, with farmers lining up to secure supply. With its first commercial-scale facility breaking ground in Delhi, California, Nitricity is scaling globally to meet surging demand from organic growers in the US and Europe. Why we invested in Nitricity The climate case: Conventional fertilizers made through the Haber-Bosch process are responsible for ~2% of global GHG emissions, while also degrading soils, polluting waterways, and driving biodiversity loss. Worse, up to 70% of nitrogen applied is lost to the environment 1 . Nitricity’s organic, circular alternative cuts emissions by more than 90% and restores soil health, while replacing animal-based fertilizers with a cleaner, safer option. The business case: Nitricity is addressing the $150B global fertilizer market, starting with a beachhead in organic nitrogen fertilizer for high-value crops, a segment worth over $11B on its own 2 . Farmers are eager for better, affordable solutions, and Nitricity delivers. Its product flows seamlessly through irrigation systems, avoids clogging, and enables more efficient nitrogen use, cutting input costs. With over $150m already in its sales pipeline and binding offtake agreements stretching through 2028, Nitricity is scaling from proven demand, not speculative adoption. The company’s Series B raise, closed in the third quarter of 2025, will accelerate US expansion, advance R&D, and build the European customer pipeline and partnerships in preparation for international growth. The team: Founded in 2018 by Stanford graduates Dr. Nicolas Pinkowski (CEO), Dr. Joshua McEnaney (President & CTO), and Dr. Jay Schwalbe (CSO), Nitricity began with a solar-powered experiment on a lemon tree. Today, the founders lead a 38-person team with deep scientific expertise, a clear commercial track record, and a bold vision for circular, plant-based fertilizer production. Their entrepreneurial grit, coupled with strategic backing from leading climate and agri-tech investors, positions Nitricity as a future global leader in sustainable fertilizer. name: NZN
description: Net Zero Nitrogen (NZN) is pioneering a new generation of sustainable agriculture with its breakthrough biofertilizer solution. The UK-based agtech company is developing a novel bioinoculant using naturally occurring endophytic bacteria that colonize crops to reduce the need for synthetic nitrogen fertilizers (SNFs). Unlike most alternatives, NZN’s solution is non-GM, requires no new machinery, and is easy to apply. It offers farmers a “green discount”: lower costs with higher yields and reduced emissions. NZN has already shown strong traction in ASEAN, where it is preparing to scale with the support of major climate-focused investors. Why we invested in NZN The climate case: Synthetic nitrogen fertilizers are responsible for ~2% of global GHG emissions (1.13 Gt CO₂e) and are a leading source of nitrous oxide, a greenhouse gas nearly 300 times more potent than CO₂. The production and overuse of SNFs also damages soil microbiomes, pollutes waterways, and drives biodiversity loss. NZN’s bioinoculant technology delivers up to 88% fewer emissions during production and mitigates downstream pollution. This makes it a powerful lever for climate mitigation in agriculture, a sector often overlooked in decarbonisation. The business case: NZN is entering a $200B global fertilizer market with a solution that’s both more sustainable and more cost-effective. The product requires no regulatory exemptions, no GM approval, and no farmer behavior change. It’s already generating significant traction in ASEAN markets through multiple proof-of-concept trials and interest from major agri-input distributors. With minimal transmission loss and no nitrous oxide leakage, NZN offers not just a green premium, but a green discount. The team: CEO Justin Hughes brings entrepreneurial vision and leadership experience as a former Red Arrows pilot, while CSO Dr. Gary Devine leads scientific development with deep biological expertise. Together with co-founder Alan Burbidge, the NZN team combines scientific rigour and strategic execution, positioning the company to transform one of agriculture’s most polluting inputs.
